hook: You haven't been bad at reading people. You've been untrained. Those are not the same thing.
topic: Skills gap vs. character flaw — reframing the ability to read people as learnable
body:
**You haven't been bad at reading people. You've been untrained. And those are not the same thing — because one is a character flaw and the other is a skills gap, and only one of them is fixable.**

Most people were never taught how to observe another person. Not really. We were taught social behaviour — how to be polite, how to make eye contact at the right moments, how to perform attentiveness. But not perceptual behaviour. Not what to actually look for beneath the words.

So what happens is: you walk around with a signal receiver but no manual. You pick things up — you feel them — but without a framework to interpret them, they just become noise. Or anxiety. Or the thing you dismiss because you don't want to be the person who sees problems everywhere.

Being wrong about people in the past isn't evidence that you lack the ability to read them. It's evidence that you've been applying an untrained skill without a system behind it. That's a very different problem.

Perceptiveness is trainable. Your nervous system already knows how to receive the signals. What you're building is the framework to interpret them correctly — to stop dismissing the real ones and stop overweighting the noisy ones.

You're not broken. You're just at the beginning of something learnable.

Full framework in the link in my bio.
